project.title: Example Capability Vocabulary
project.description: A built-in demonstration ontology that shows how to configure OCG for one vocabulary-oriented GitHub Pages site per fork.

examples.label: Basic Capability Example
examples.description: Smallest useful graph that exercises the core classes and properties.

examples.label: Advanced Capability Example
examples.description: More expressive example showing multiple constraints, labels, and concept references.

hero.headline: A config-first companion site for one ontology per repository.
hero.body: This default repository content is a working test/example. Replace the files in source/, update this config document, and the build regenerates the GitHub Pages site around your ontology.

resourcePanel.title: Published Artifacts
resourcePanel.body: Every linked artifact below is derived from the configured source package and exposed through a static site that can be deployed directly with GitHub Actions.

overviewCards.title: Replace the Example Source
overviewCards.body: Swap the built-in ontology, shapes, examples, and specification with your own files, keeping the same source/ directory structure or updating the config paths.

overviewCards.title: Customize the Website
overviewCards.body: Colors, hero text, featured terms, raw viewer tabs, and custom narrative sections all come from ocg.config.json.

overviewCards.title: Publish with GitHub Pages
overviewCards.body: The included workflow rebuilds the site and deploys the generated output directory on every push to main.

customSections.title: How This Example Helps
customSections.body: The default files intentionally exercise each major surface of the template so new users can inspect a working ontology, SHACL file, ShEx schema, examples, spec page, graph, reference page, and per-term HTML output before replacing anything.
items: The ontology declares classes, object properties, datatype properties, annotation properties, and SKOS concepts.
The examples use the declared terms so the term pages show realistic cross-links.
The config demonstrates featured terms, viewer tab selection, custom cards, and footer text.

footer.secondary: Edit ocg.config.json and the source/ files to adapt this repo to your own vocabulary.
